title: E-waste rare element recovery economics
bottleneck: Printed circuit boards contain gold, palladium, and rare earths at concentrations above many ores, but recovering them economically is unsolved: shredding mixes everything into low-grade streams, manual disassembly is too costly in high-wage countries, and hydrometallurgical recovery of trace elements from complex mixtures is chemical-intensive. Most e-waste is still smelted for copper and gold while the rest is lost.
why_it_blocks: Demand for electronics metals keeps growing while ore grades decline; urban mining could supply a large fraction. Without economic recovery, critical elements dissipate into landfills and slag, forcing ever more destructive primary mining.
current_state: Automated disassembly with robotics and AI sorting is improving, and dedicated e-waste refineries recover an expanding element list. But collection rates remain low — most e-waste never reaches a recycler — and the economics still depend on gold and copper subsidizing the rest.
